title: Intake
does: The Script Coordinator, the Director's assistant, goes through everything you put in — notes, references, any drafts — and writes down what it establishes in the three files the room works from: the people, the world, the story. Then, in passes of their own, it lists what is still open and offers you options for each.
asks: Is this what your material says? Then answer the open items: approve an option, edit it, or leave it for the room. Run intake again and it folds your answers into the files and leaves only what is still open.

title: Visual check
does: The Script Coordinator writes five to eight visual briefs from the four settled files, the room renders each one, and the Coordinator holds every picture up against its brief. Text is canon; a picture is a way to see it, and a way to catch a misreading before production makes it expensive.
asks: Does this look like the world, the people, the technology and the scale the files describe? Keep, send back or reject each image. What a brief could not find in the files is now an open item.

title: Development
does: Decide what the book is: the brief, and what the three files leave open — the world, the plot, the people.
asks: Is this the right story, told by these people?

title: Audition
does: Two writers write the same opening pages. You pick the voice.
asks: Whose book do you want to read?

title: Writing
does: The writer you picked writes the whole script.

title: Execution
does: Lay out and letter every page until the pages pass the readiness check. Then the page prompts are written.
asks: Review the pages: keep them, note them, send them back, or finalize.
